At the violating step everything is red — so I'll walk backwards to find the truncated yellow.
Green at step 90, red by 94 — I'll check each intermediate step.
Yellow shows for only 2 steps instead of 4. I'll map the gap-out and check the earlier violation.
Yellow lasted only 2s versus required 4s. I'll trace the phase history to see what cut it short.
Yellow observed only at steps 92-93. I'll examine earlier history to understand the phase transition cause.
I see a long-waiting NS direction alongside the short yellow — I'll gather a bit more timing evidence.
EW green ran long while NS waited ~70s before the yellow was cut to 2s. I'll locate when that green began.
Yellow was truncated to 2s while the opposing direction had waited ~70s — looks like actuated recall cutting yellow short. Testing with fixed-time control.
